logline: A single mother running a side-dish shop becomes romantically entangled with South Korea's most famous hagwon math instructor - inside the brutal machinery of the college-entrance exam industry.

renewal.note: Single-season run of 16 episodes concluded March 5, 2023. No sequel announced.

bollymeter.basis: A 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 8 critics, inclusion in TIME Magazine's 10 Best Korean Dramas of 2023 on Netflix, and a finale rating of 17.0 percent - among the strongest tvN closers of the year - confirm a show that delivered on every level of its satirical premise.

pull_quotes.text: A breath of fresh air that stands out among Korean romantic dramas.

seasons.review_body: Crash Course in Romance aired on tvN from January 14 to March 5, 2023, written by Yang Hee-seung and directed by Yoo Je-won. Its satirical scope sets it apart from standard K-drama rom-com: the show uses the romance between a banchan shop owner and a celebrity hagwon instructor to autopsy the Korean education industry's class dynamics, parental anxiety, and the violence inflicted on teenagers by a system built around one exam. TIME Magazine included it in the 10 Best Korean Dramas of 2023 on Netflix. Eight critics on Rotten Tomatoes awarded a unanimous 100 percent. Viewership grew from an opening 4.0 percent to a series-best 17.0 percent in the finale, and topped Good Data Corporation's TV Topicality chart for four consecutive weeks. Jeon Do-yeon and Jung Kyung-ho were praised across the board for a pairing that operates as equals. The 93 percent Popcornmeter and IMDb 7.7 reflect an audience that found the social critique landing without didacticism.

episode_reviews.title: You and I, the Intersection of Two Universes
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere sets up both worlds in parallel: the hagwon ecosystem rendered with satirical precision, and Haeng-seon's banchan world as its unpretentious counterweight. The two leads' antagonistic first meeting works because neither character is positioned as obviously right.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Choi Chi-yeol walks into a side-dish shop looking for the one variety of side dish that actually made him eat during a competition - and the encounter is both absurd and oddly touching.

episode_reviews.title: Point of Intersection between Comedy and Tragedy
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The title announces the episode's formal achievement: the show holds its satirical comedy and its genuinely dark portrait of exam-industry harm in the same frame without letting either register as false. Audience discussions consistently cited this as the season's tonal peak.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A student's breakdown inside the exam prep circuit forces both leads to confront what their work costs the people it is supposed to serve.

episode_reviews.title: You and I, the Union of Two Universes
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale pulled 17.0 percent nationwide, the series best. It pays off both the personal arc and the social argument without softening either. Each title in the series referenced a mathematical concept; the finale's 'union' mirrors the premiere's 'intersection' with deliberate structural symmetry.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The closing image reverses the geometry of episode one - the same two people, the same space, an entirely different equation.
